add.header: Pure-logic helpers isolated from hardware for testability
add.description: card_format, card_identity, bench_math, ui_geometry, and touch_calibration are each kept as narrow, single-purpose header/cpp pairs with explicit 'no hardware/Arduino dependency, safe to unit-test on host' documentation, avoiding a generic-utils dumping ground while still being genuinely reused across hardware/, benchmark/, and ui/.

add.header: Shared helpers earn their abstraction via real multi-site reuse
add.description: recordSdError(), allocateDmaBuffer(), and runChunkedIo() each replace concrete duplicated logic that existed before the prior review round's fixes (2-5 real call sites each), rather than being introduced speculatively.

add.header: Internal headers keep public module APIs minimal
add.description: display_ui_internal.h and benchmark_internal.h hold only what's shared across a module's own .cpp files and are explicitly marked 'not part of the public API', so display_ui.h and benchmark.h stay small and consistent instead of exposing implementation details.

add.header: Header comments document contract asymmetry to prevent leaky assumptions
add.description: sd_card.h explains, in the doc comment on scanCard(), why it returns a bool over persistent global state instead of a self-contained result like runSpiScalingBenchmark()'s SpiScaleResult, so callers can't mistakenly treat the two APIs as interchangeable.

add.header: No classes, interfaces, or facades in this procedural codebase
add.description: The project is built entirely from free functions and static file-scope state (a deliberate embedded-C++ module pattern), so delegation-heavy-class, one-implementation-interface, and facade/re-export anti-patterns have no surface to occur on.

add.header: Two-library dependency set, each with a single clear purpose
add.description: platformio.ini's [env:cyd] declares only TFT_eSPI (display) and SdFat (SD/filesystem) -- no overlapping or redundant libraries exist, and Arduino's built-in SD.h/FS.h are never used alongside SdFat, so there is no split-purpose duplication to reconcile.

add.header: No dependency manifest drift or stale lock artifacts
add.description: platformio.ini is the only dependency manifest in the repo (no package.json/library.json at root); the fetched-library cache under .pio/ is gitignored, so there is nothing checked in that could go stale relative to the manifest.

add.header: Platform toolchain version left unpinned
add.description: [env:cyd]'s `platform = espressif32` has no version suffix, unlike the two lib_deps entries which were pinned in a prior fix round; this is the one remaining place a fresh build could silently pick up a different toolchain.

add.header: Shared runChunkedIo() eliminated write/read/verify triplication
add.description: benchmark.cpp's timedFileWrite/timedFileRead/verifyFile now all call one runChunkedIo() helper parameterized by a ChunkIoFn callback (chunkWrite/chunkRead/chunkReadAndCrc) and a void* context; only progress-label and rate-display differ per call site, confirming the historical low_level_elegance fix has held.

add.header: uiShowSpiScaleResult decomposed into named single-purpose helpers
add.description: display_results.cpp splits the former ~185-line function into scaleGraphMaxSpeed/drawScaleGraphFrame/scalePointCoords/drawScalePoint/buildScaleSummary, each documented and independently readable; the orchestrator is now a short loop over these helpers, confirming the historical fix has held.

add.header: Guard clauses appear only at genuine boundaries
add.description: Null/failure checks are limited to real boundary conditions (DMA allocation failure, sd.card() absence, zero sector count, card.cardOk) rather than being sprinkled defensively on values that can't be null, keeping edge-case handling precise without sprawl.

add.header: scanCard()'s four-stage qualification loop repeats a fail/record/continue shape
add.description: Each of cardBegin/readCID/readCSD/readSector follows the same 3-line failure pattern; this mirrors the actual sequential hardware protocol rather than being copy-paste drift, so further extraction would obscure the stage ordering rather than clarify it.

add.header: Single shared app_types.h for all cross-module data shapes
add.description: CardInfo, AttemptResult, BenchmarkResult, and SpiScaleResult/SpiScalePoint are defined once in src/core/app_types.h and passed by const-reference across hardware/, benchmark/, and ui/ with no per-module duplicate or adapter structs — the one obvious place boundary data is shaped.

add.header: Pure translation helpers isolated from hardware, each unit-tested
add.description: card_format, card_identity, ui_geometry, bench_math, and touch_calibration each hold one module's boundary-crossing translation logic (byte/clock formatting, vendor/stage lookups, hit-testing, coordinate mapping) in files explicitly marked hardware-independent and mirrored by a test/test_<name> host test — translation happens in one obvious, verifiable place rather than being inlined at call sites.

add.header: Uniform draw()/hitTest() pairing convention across UI screens
add.description: Every interactive screen (Home, BenchMenu) exposes a uiDraw*()/uiHitTest*(x,y) pair returning a plain enum action, letting main.cpp's orchestration loops treat every screen identically — a predictable, unsurprising handoff shape reused rather than reinvented per screen.

add.header: Boundary side effects documented at the declaration, not just in commit history
add.description: scanCard()'s getter-vs-return-value design and runSpiScalingBenchmark()'s hidden rescan are both explained directly in sd_card.h/benchmark.h doc comments (why persistent state fits one use case and a one-shot result fits the other), so the previously-flagged undocumented side effects are now durably visible to any future reader, not just fixed once.

add.header: benchmark/ calls directly into ui/ for live progress display
add.description: runChunkedIo()/runQuickBenchmark() in benchmark.cpp call uiShowProgress() directly rather than the orchestrator (main.cpp) mediating progress updates, the only benchmark->ui edge in the import graph. This is a pragmatic choice for a single-threaded embedded loop (no callback/async machinery needed) but is a real exception to the otherwise consistent main-as-composer pattern.

add.header: Full test coverage of the project's own pure-logic surface
add.description: Every module CLAUDE.md and platformio.ini classify as hardware-independent (bench_math, card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration, ui_geometry, app_types) has a matching Unity suite in test/, and .github/workflows/native-tests.yml runs pio test -e native on every push/PR, making this an enforced rather than aspirational safety net.

add.header: Tests assert real edge cases, not happy-path smoke checks
add.description: Test suites verify boundary conditions (exact 1 GiB threshold, half-open hit-test rectangles, out-of-range touch clamping, chunk-split CRC32 equivalence, count==0 zero-max division), giving genuine regression protection rather than just confirming functions run.

add.header: Honest documentation of the untested hardware-coupled surface
add.description: CLAUDE.md explicitly names which files have no automated coverage (main.cpp, hardware/ SPI/touch code, benchmark/ SdFat I/O, ui/ TFT_eSPI rendering) and states why (no mock Arduino/SdFat/TFT_eSPI layer exists), so the coverage gap is a known, calibrated tradeoff rather than a hidden one.

add.header: display_results.cpp pure-math helpers untested, breaking established extraction
add.description: scaleGraphMaxSpeed()/scalePointCoords()/buildScaleSummary() are pure logic added during a prior refactor but left in the TFT-coupled file instead of ui_geometry.cpp, the codebase's own established home for such host-testable math -- see issue untested_pure_logic_in_display_results.

add.header: Uniform bool+out-ref shape for fallible reads
add.description: readTouch() and rawReadAtCurrentSpeed() both signal success via a bool return with the result written to a trailing reference parameter, so a developer who has seen one fallible hardware-read function can predict the shape of the other without checking its implementation.

add.header: Uniform (inputs, char* out, size_t outSize) shape for string producers
add.description: formatHumanBytes(), formatSpiClock(), and buildScaleSummary() are the only string-producing functions in the codebase and all three use the identical bounded-buffer output pattern -- consistent with embedded/no-heap constraints and predictable across call sites.

add.header: No overloads, no >5-param public functions
add.description: Across all 13 public headers, no function name is overloaded and the widest public signature (scalePointCoords, 5 params) stays at the documented threshold -- there is no evidence of argument-type-based interface overloading anywhere in the public surface.

add.header: scanCard()/runSpiScalingBenchmark() shape divergence remains, now fully document
add.description: The previously-flagged shape mismatch between scanCard()'s persistent-getter model and runSpiScalingBenchmark()'s self-contained SpiScaleResult was resolved by adding an explicit rationale comment on scanCard()'s declaration in sd_card.h rather than unifying the shapes; this is a legitimate and sufficient resolution since the two functions serve genuinely different access patterns (queryable history vs. one-shot display), but scanCard()'s bool return staying unused at every call site is a small

add.header: No authorization surface exists in this firmware
add.description: CYD SD Tester is single-user embedded firmware for a physical microSD diagnostic device: it has no network stack, no server, no user accounts/sessions, and no data store, so there are no routes, permission literals, or trust boundaries for auth consistency to apply to. This is a structural fact about the project, not a gap.

add.header: Header comments explain WHY, not WHAT
add.description: The headers with the highest mechanical comment_ratio (sd_card.h, benchmark.h, card_identity.h, touch_calibration.h, ui_geometry.h) use their comments to document non-obvious cross-file design decisions -- e.g. sd_card.h contrasts scanCard()'s persistent-state getter pattern against runSpiScalingBenchmark()'s one-shot return value, and touch_calibration.h documents the physical X/Y axis swap from panel mounting. None of it restates adjacent code, so the high comment density is a documentation st

add.header: Diagnostic Serial output is purposeful, not nosy logging
add.description: Serial.printf calls in sd_card.cpp, benchmark.cpp, and spi_scale_benchmark.cpp print card/benchmark reports that are the tool's actual user-facing output (this is an SD diagnostic utility whose only UI besides the TFT is Serial). There is no per-function entry/exit logging or full-struct dumping; the previously-flagged unconditional touch-coordinate debug prints in touch.cpp remain removed.

add.header: recordSdError() still centralizes error-capture boilerplate
add.description: sd_card.cpp's scanCard() and spi_scale_benchmark.cpp both call the shared recordSdError(sd, errorCode, errorData, label) helper instead of duplicating the sdErrorCode()/sdErrorData()/printf pattern inline -- confirms the prior review-round fix for this dimension has held.

add.header: No migration debt markers anywhere in src/
add.description: A repo-wide search for TODO/FIXME/DEPRECATED/legacy/migrate/shim across src/ and test/ returns zero hits; the only such markers in the whole working tree live in third-party .pio/libdeps sources, not project code.

add.header: Prior README-documented migrations are fully executed
add.description: README.md's version history describes the BENCH/SCALE menu merge, the filesystemBytes->filesystemDataBytes rename, and removal of dead experimental raw-benchmark toggles; grepping for each old name/symbol confirms none remain in src/, so these are completed migrations, not ongoing ones with residue.

add.header: Dual SPI speed tables are a documented permanent split, not stale duplication
add.description: core/config.h's SPI_SPEEDS (normal qualification, 20/10/4/1MHz) and SPI_SCALE_SPEEDS (diagnostic scaling benchmark, 40/20/10/4/1MHz) look like they could be an incomplete consolidation, but README.md's v0.7.1 notes and adjacent code comments explain the 40MHz split is intentional and permanent (normal scans stopped trusting 40MHz; the scaling benchmark keeps probing it as a diagnostic data point).

add.header: util/ dumping ground fully eliminated
add.description: The previously-flagged util/ directory (card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration living outside their sole-consumer domain while bench_math/ui_geometry stayed in-domain) no longer exists; all three were folded into hardware/, its only consumer, making the pure/testable-helper placement rule consistent across benchmark/, hardware/, and ui/.

add.header: core/ is a genuine acyclic shared kernel
add.description: core/app_types.h and core/config.h have zero outgoing includes beyond each other and the standard library, and are the only two files with avg_fan_in >= 5 imported from every other domain (hardware, benchmark, ui) -- exactly the root-level-core exception the package_organization rubric calls out to skip.

add.header: Consistent private internal-header pattern
add.description: benchmark/benchmark_internal.h and ui/display_ui_internal.h both serve the same role -- sharing helpers across sibling .cpp files in one folder without exposing them on the public header -- applied identically in both domains rather than one folder inventing its own convention.

add.header: benchmark/ depends on ui/ for progress reporting
add.description: benchmark.cpp includes ui/display_ui.h and calls uiShowProgress() directly from its I/O loop, the only coupling_matrix edge that does not point toward core/; this contradicts the one-directional layering the codebase documents for itself in benchmark_internal.h (hardware/ deliberately cannot depend on benchmark/). See issue benchmark_depends_on_ui.

add.header: Linear, single-site boot sequence in main.cpp
add.description: setup() calls initDisplay(), initTouch(), initSdHardware(), then rescan() in a flat, unconditional sequence with no branching or lazy/conditional init paths, so the entire hardware bring-up order is visible in one ~10-line function.

add.header: TFT singleton uses lazy function-local static
add.description: tft() in display_ui_internal.cpp wraps a function-local static TFT_eSPI instance instead of a file-scope global, so the object is constructed on first use rather than at ambiguous cross-TU static-init time — this sidesteps static-initialization-order-fiasco risk even though the codebase has only one entry point.

add.header: SD hardware globals gated by state flags, not call order
add.description: sd_card.cpp exposes its SdFs/CardInfo/AttemptResult statics only through getSd()/getCardInfo()/getAttempts(), and every consumer (runQuickBenchmark, rawReadAtCurrentSpeed, removeTestFile) checks cardOk/volumeOk/sd.card() before use rather than assuming initSdHardware()/scanCard() already ran — misordering degrades gracefully (early return) instead of crashing.

add.header: Eager vs. lazy singleton construction style differs across modules
add.description: sd_card.cpp's hardware globals (sd, info, attempts, cid, csd) are plain file-scope statics built at C++ static-init time, while display_ui_internal.cpp's TFT_eSPI instance is built lazily inside its accessor function — both are safe given the single-entry-point boot sequence, but the pattern choice isn't consistent across the two singleton call sites.

add.header: Shared chunked-I/O helper in benchmark.cpp
add.description: runChunkedIo() takes a ChunkIoFn function pointer plus void* context and drives the shared read/write/progress loop; timedFileWrite/timedFileRead/verifyFile each just supply the chunk operation and stage labels instead of duplicating the loop, replacing what a prior review flagged as triplicated code.

add.header: scanCard() decomposed into single-purpose steps
add.description: fillCardIdentity(), runConsistencyChecks(), and printCardReport() are extracted out of scanCard() (src/hardware/sd_card.cpp), so the orchestrator reads as a sequence of named steps rather than one monolithic function mixing qualification, identity parsing, consistency checks, and reporting.

add.header: Explicit callback threading avoids an upward dependency
add.description: BenchmarkProgressFn (benchmark_internal.h) is passed explicitly into runQuickBenchmark() from main.cpp rather than benchmark/ #including ui/display_ui.h directly; the header comment documents this is deliberate so benchmark/ does not depend upward on ui/. This is a design decision that trades one extra parameter for a cleaner dependency direction.

add.header: scanCard/runSpiScalingBenchmark scaffold duplication remains, accepted
add.description: The two speed-iterating routines still share a near-identical reset+cardBegin+per-speed-error-logging scaffold. This was already reviewed and marked wontfix on the grounds that with only two call sites the duplication is tolerable; still present in the current code, not a new or newly-reportable defect.

add.header: Side-effect contracts documented at declaration site
add.description: scanCard() and runSpiScalingBenchmark() both carry multi-line comments at their header declarations explaining hidden global-state mutation and exactly what a caller may assume about getCardInfo()/getSd() afterward -- this is the strongest positive pattern in the dimension and appears to be a direct result of a prior review round.

add.header: getX() naming matches purity everywhere
add.description: Every getX()-named function found (getCardInfo, getSd, getAttempts, getAttemptCount) is a pure read of static module state with no side effects; no getter-that-mutates pattern exists in this codebase.

add.header: benchmark.h documents one sibling function, not the other
add.description: runSpiScalingBenchmark() has an exhaustive side-effect comment while runQuickBenchmark(), in the same header, has none despite comparable failure-path and I/O side-effect complexity -- an isolated documentation-coverage gap rather than a systemic pattern.

add.header: Write-only status fields in CardInfo/BenchmarkResult
add.description: cleanupOk (BenchmarkResult) and csdOk (CardInfo) are set but never read by any consumer, and cleanupOk's default-true polarity breaks the false-by-default convention every sibling *Ok field follows -- a minor struct-contract inconsistency isolated to two fields.

add.header: Consistent guard-clause control flow
add.description: Failure handling across scanCard(), runQuickBenchmark(), rawReadAtCurrentSpeed(), removeTestFile(), and runSpiScalingBenchmark() uniformly uses early-return guard clauses rather than nested conditionals, so a developer can trust that once a failure check fires, nothing further in that function runs.

add.header: Shared chunked-I/O loop removes triplicated control flow
add.description: runChunkedIo() in benchmark.cpp is the single control-flow path driving the write, read, and CRC-verify passes via a ChunkIoFn function pointer, so the three benchmark stages cannot silently diverge in looping/progress/error-handling behavior the way three hand-copied loops could.

add.header: CardInfo::csdOk is dead write-only state
add.description: csdOk is always set true in lockstep with cidOk inside fillCardIdentity() but is never read by any production code path (only cidOk gates behavior in printCardReport()/identityCheckName()); it exists as a vestigial twin of cidOk from what looks like partial CSD-support wiring.

add.header: Enum classes are never bypassed with raw literals
add.description: AttemptStage, HomeAction, and BenchMenuAction are all enum class types and every comparison/switch site in card_identity.cpp, display_diagnostics.cpp, display_ui.cpp, and main.cpp uses the typed enumerator, never an underlying int — confirmed by exhaustive grep across src/ with no bare-int comparisons against these fields.

add.header: SdFat macro constants intentionally kept as uint8_t, not wrapped
add.description: CardInfo.cardType and .fsType stay uint8_t because SdFat's SD_CARD_TYPE_*/FAT_TYPE_* are plain library-defined macros, not a C++ enum the project owns; sd_card.h documents this rationale inline and cardTypeName()/fsName() both switch on the macro values with a default case, so the classification is centralized despite the loose storage type.

add.header: Explicit casts before printf integer format specifiers
add.description: Every uint32_t/uint64_t value passed to a %lu/%08lX-style specifier is explicitly cast to (unsigned long) at the call site (sd_card.cpp, benchmark.cpp, benchmark_raw.cpp, display_results.cpp) instead of relying on an implicit conversion, which keeps the printf calls portable and warning-free.

add.header: Cast convention fully unified to C-style casts
add.description: A prior review round found one stray static_cast in card_format.cpp against an otherwise all-C-style-cast codebase; a full grep of src/ for static_cast|reinterpret_cast|dynamic_cast now returns zero matches, confirming the cleanup held and the convention is uniform.
